targetText: The general rise in the rate of wages would, therefore, after a temporary disturbance of market prices, only result in a general fall of the rate of profit without any permanent change in the prices of commodities.
explanation: This is Marx's central rebuttal to Weston: wages rising does not simply raise prices and cancel out the gain. It reduces the rate of profit instead. Workers benefit at the expense of capitalists, not consumers.

targetText: Capital and labour would be transferred from the less remunerative to the more remunerative branches; and this process of transfer would go on until the supply in the one department of industry would have risen proportionately to the increased demand
explanation: Marx describes how capital mobility between industries re-equalizes profit rates after a wage rise, redistributing production toward necessities. This shows that market adjustments absorb the change in distribution, not prices.
